subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Decentralized Social Media
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Decentralized Social Media.

hook.text: What if no single company owned your social network? Decentralized platforms are trying to make that real.

buildup.text: Mastodon, Bluesky, and the Fediverse let users join servers run by communities, not corporations.

discovery.text: On decentralized platforms, you own your data, choose your algorithm, and can move servers without losing followers.

twist.text: Decentralized platforms struggle to attract mainstream users. Network effects still favor the incumbents.

climax.text: Decentralization offers freedom from corporate control — if enough people choose principle over convenience.

punchline.text: No corporation in control. If people choose it.

quiz.question: What is the main advantage of decentralized social media?
options: Users own their data and no single company controls the platform
They have more users than traditional platforms
